output.title: Why subscription sprawl survives in small teams
output.body:
Subscription sprawl survives in small teams for a boring reason: it sits inside background admin. A tool gets signed up for, then the review gets pushed behind invoices, renewals, and everything else that feels more urgent. So the real problem is usually visibility, not the software itself.

For a 1–10 person business, I would treat this as a workflow decision, not a cleanup project. Ask one blunt question: can you list every active subscription and its renewal date right now? If not, the first step is a one-time manual audit. Get the list into one place, then decide whether you want simple renewal reminders, a searchable register, or a quarterly review to keep it honest.

That is the kind of bounded workflow Bareni looks for: one recurring task, one clear owner, one control. If the list is already small and tidy, a spreadsheet may be enough. If it is messy, start with the audit first and only then decide whether a simple workflow built with AI plus a spreadsheet is worth scoping. Human approval still stays in charge for any cancellation or payment step.
